# Othryn administrative automation 1.0.0

Canonical source: `othryn-stack/tools/ci-cd/automation/`. Each repository vendors the same Node.js files under `.github/scripts/automation/`; runtime never checks out another private repository. `.github/automation.config.json` is the repository-specific schema version 1 profile. Change the canonical source, run the offline tests, then distribute the reviewed version to each repository together. Do not edit a single vendored engine without updating the canonical version and distribution.

## Credentials and optional integrations

- GitHub administration uses the scoped job `GITHUB_TOKEN`. No new PAT is needed. Secret-bearing jobs execute only immutable base/default automation; no pull-request head code, package scripts or dependencies execute there.
- Jira accepts the existing `JIRA_AUTH` secret (base64 `email:API-token`) or the pair `JIRA_EMAIL` and `JIRA_API_TOKEN`. Missing credentials fail explicitly on a valid Jira task; HTTP errors and non-JSON responses fail without printing response bodies or secrets.
- Chat release planning accepts `version` and optional `release_date` through New Release Cycle on main. A single active release with the exact repository prefix is selected automatically. If more than one exists, set the non-secret repository variable `JIRA_RELEASE_NAME`; nothing attempts to write Actions variables with insufficient permissions.
- GitHub Projects remains opt-in. LocalCameraServer preserves project 4 as configuration, disabled initially. To enable it, review `projects.enabled=true` in the profile, set `ENABLE_PROJECTS=true`, and provide the pre-existing `PROJECT_TOKEN` with access to that project. No token is invented or broadened automatically.

## Ownership and Jira boundaries

Branch Created starts an unambiguous AR/SP ticket only for a branch created by an authorized repository writer. Tags are ignored. PR Pipeline owns the managed Jira link, optional author assignment, registry of associated PRs, planned release tracking, and lifecycle updates. PR Health Check owns warnings, health labels and a single updated checklist. User descriptions and PR titles are preserved. Legacy Asana and duplicate PR owners are removed.

Draft PRs begin In Progress. Ready PRs move forward to PR in Review; development merges move to PR Merged. Retries and conversion to draft never reset a later status or overwrite an existing start date. Epic and QA issue types, parents and unrelated tickets are never transitioned. Existing required-label profiles retain their label check; reviewer requests, approval of the current commit, branch drift and size remain visible. Review submission and dismissal refresh only PR Health, without Jira secrets or lifecycle transitions, using immutable base automation and fresh PR identity checks.

## Production acceptance and releases

Deploy Production emits `production-deployment-evidence/production-deployment-evidence.json` only after deployment and health success. The consumer re-fetches the exact producer run and workflow identity, permits push or normal manual deployment on main, validates repository/SHA/run/environment/health, and reads only one bounded JSON file from a bounded ZIP. It never extracts or executes artifact code. Missing evidence after skipped/first-start jobs is deferred.

The explicit jobs are verify-production -> publish-release -> finalize-jira. Every job revalidates the same producer event, with no dependency on a release event generated by `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Only SensorServer, which already published releases, has GitHub release publication enabled; other consumers do not invent tags. Draft release candidates target an immutable development SHA and never delete releases. Jira fixVersions are added idempotently. Done additionally requires Ready for Deployment/Resolved and complete visibility of associated merged PRs. Multi-repository tickets, including the AR-2920 cohort, require explicit production acceptance by their owner and remain deferred; merged development PRs cannot prove deployment of every service.

All runtime network operations are explicit in `runner.mjs`. Offline tests inject mocked clients and never call Jira/GitHub. Run `node --test .github/scripts/automation/*.test.mjs` from a repository. A successful local suite proves the contract and regressions, not the availability of live credentials, remote transitions, or a successful deployment.
